correctness.rationale: A theorem for arbitrary shore sizes reduces exactly to 3375 nonempty color-support triples, whose full color-labelled trajectories are checked exhaustively through time seven. Every original vertex is governed by its starting shore/color representative. The finite complete table yields F^7=F^3, exact period-one/period-four classification, 54 and 619 recurrent colored-support patterns, and the 20 coefficient entries, each weighted by exact inclusion-exclusion surjection counts. Independently coded microscopic graph updates reproduce all predicted classifications on 173376 configurations and the sharp K_{1,1,2} witness. The finite quotient is an all-graph-size proof step; small graph tests are only cross-checks.

originality.rationale: No equivalent exact four-color complete-tripartite global-iterate identity or all-size orbit polynomial was found. The 1991 Fisch–Gravner–Griffeath source gives general multicolor rules but treats primarily planar lattice wave phenomenology; the 2016 Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff source proves results only for three colors. Contrasting two-shore four-color periods include six, so those results do not imply the sharp three-shore period collapse. Remaining possibility of historical undocumented equivalence is explicitly acknowledged.

value.rationale: A whole infinite natural graph family is fully classified by actual temporal periods, with a sharp finite transient uniform in all shore sizes, explicit sixteen-term primitive-orbit polynomial, and a decisive topology-induced removal of period six seen on bicliques. Two-cycles of the quotient lifting to four-cycles explain a genuine dynamical subtlety beyond raw counting. This is a complete natural invariant, not an arbitrary finite sample or a standard renaming.
